verdict: Verizon added 406,000 postpaid phone customers — its best third quarter in five years — and record adjusted EBITDA let it raise full-year guidance for a third straight quarter.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $1.17 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.31

kpis.label: Postpaid phone net adds
kpis.note: best Q3 in five years; 137K net account adds, best in a decade

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Phones, home internet and devices for households — mobility and broadband service of $19,777M, wireless equipment of $4,277M and other revenue of $2,378M. The segment earned $8,093M of operating income.

segments.name: Business
segments.note: Wireless and wireline services for companies, governments and wholesale customers. The segment earned $855M of operating income, up 19%.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Device insurance programs, businesses held for sale (including the international wireline business moved here in Q2 2026) and the remainder to consolidated revenue after intersegment eliminations.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling phones and plans, stores, marketing and running the company — down 4% as promotional spending was cut.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the network, spectrum-related assets and equipment over their lives — up 10%.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $1,950M and $122M of profit belonging to noncontrolling interests, partly offset by $120M of other income; part-owned businesses lost $3M (the equityM line). The flow lands on the $5,198M attributable to Verizon — consolidated net income was $5,320M.
footerNote: Cost of revenue combines Verizon's reported cost of services ($7,265M) and cost of wireless equipment ($5,823M); operating expenses are SG&A and depreciation & amortization, matching Verizon's income statement. Consumer and Business revenues are as reported by segment; Corporate & other is the remainder to consolidated revenue.

takeaways.title: Customers came back
takeaways.text: Verizon added 406,000 postpaid phone customers and 137,000 net accounts — the best account growth in over a decade — while postpaid phone churn improved to 0.94% and promotional acquisition costs fell 41%.

takeaways.title: Service revenue is the engine
takeaways.text: Mobility and broadband service revenue grew 2.9% to $23.5B. Equipment revenue fell 9% as people keep phones longer and Verizon spends less on device subsidies — a deliberate trade for margin: adjusted EBITDA hit a record $13.8B.

takeaways.title: An AI infrastructure bet
takeaways.text: Verizon signed a $2B+ deal with Amazon Web Services to scale distributed compute for AI workloads over its fiber network — and raised full-year guidance for postpaid adds, adjusted EPS and free cash flow for the third straight quarter.
